annotations.title: The man hath appeared.
annotations.text: Al ancient fathers and Catholique writers say, this was an Angel, which appeared in the forme of a man, and it is plaine by this text. [1] Yet some protestantes wil haue this person to be Christ, the eternal word of God. [2]Who afterwardes became man. And neuertheles where by & by (v. 16.) he admonisheth Manue to offer sacrifice to God, they note that he sought not his owne honour but Gods, whose messenger he was: either plainly contradicting themselues, or els teaching Arrianisme, as though the Sonne of God were not God; or inferiour to God the Father.

notes.text: Protestantes either contradict themselues, or teach Arrianisme.
